No usable option chain (ATM legs not two-sided), so there is no implied move; the sealed baseline is tier 'thin'. The last six prints moved the stock at the report-day close by about -6.8% (May 2025), -6.6% (Aug 2025), -10.3% (Nov 17 2025), -9.5% (Feb 26 2026), -1.6% after opening +7% (May 28 2026) and +7.2% (Aug 6 2026): five of six down, in a stock in a secular downtrend. At about 152M shares incl. pre-funded warrants the equity is about $63M against my estimate of about $48M cash at Sep 30 (own arithmetic, assumes ~$8M Q3 burn), so the stock trades near cash; the $24.3M TASE convertible held at the trustee matures 12/31/2026 and appears to sit against restricted funds rather than the $41.9M cash line.
view: The print turns on the FY26 revenue guide and the burn. The guide looks hard to hold: H1 was $1.16M and backlog was flat at about $1M at both March 31 and June 30, yet the low end needs $2.84M in H2, 2.4 times H1, and Q4 alone near $2M. The routes to that are a December 2026 SOP for the Hirain L4 program, robotaxi Phoenix orders and defense follow-on orders, all of them flagged as 'anticipated' and none confirmed since August. My best guess is a cut, or at least a firm 'low end', more likely than not. A 'low end' is already in consensus; a cut below $4M is a miss of maybe 20-30% on a revenue line analysts already set at the floor. Against that, the stock has lost 30% since the offering and 17% this week with no news. It trades near cash, so a revenue miss of about $1M on a $63M equity changes little of what the shares are worth. Management also has easy positives to show: Q3 is the first full quarter of the 15% cost cut with a sub-$7M burn target, Sept 30 cash went up on the raise, and the September L3 win and the C-UAS evaluations give the call something to talk about. The history of five down reactions in six prints says this name usually disappoints on timing, and the guide arithmetic says this one has a concrete line it can disappoint on. But the run-in and the near-cash valuation blunt it, and the size of a 13:00 move in a 92%-vol stock is mostly noise. Net: a lean down, not a bet.
unpriced: Possibly the size of the H2 ramp the guide needs. Consensus still sits at the guide's floor ($4.1M FY) from August, while backlog was flat and nothing since has confirmed the Q4 volume. The recent slide is not tied to any dated news, so it does not show the market has priced a cut below $4M. The evidence is arithmetic, not a dated datapoint, and I cannot show the cut is not already in the price, so it is a lean only.

recommendation.reason: The guide needs H2 revenue of 2.4 to 4.2 times H1 with flat backlog, so a guide cut below the $4M floor that consensus sits on is more likely than not, and five of the last six prints closed down. But the stock has already lost 30% since the September raise and 17% this week, it trades near cash, and the cost-cut and burn line is a likely positive, so I do not reach 65% that it closes lower at 13:00 on 11/19.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A reaffirmed $4-6M guide backed by a Q3 above about $1M and Q4 orders in hand (L4 SOP shipments to Hirain, robotaxi or defense orders), together with a burn under $7M.

self_critique: The cut may already be in the price. The stock is down 30% from a raise eight weeks ago and 17% this week with no news, it trades about $15M above estimated cash, and analysts already model the guide's floor. A revenue line of a few million dollars may simply not matter to a stock priced as an option on design wins. Management also has a likely good line in the burn (first full quarter of the 15% cut against a sub-$7M target) and could pair the print with an order announcement, as small caps often do. The last print rose 7%. And a 92%-vol stock at $0.42 can move 6% by 13:00 on nothing, so the direction call carries less information than its number implies.
approach_notes: P4/P6 helped: they pushed me to tie the 30% post-offering slide to dated news (there was none beyond the raise) rather than call the cut priced, and to rebuild the guide arithmetic from H1 and backlog. P7's 65 threshold kept a reasonable arithmetic lean from becoming a recommendation. With no options chain and no fresh consensus, the playbook offers little on how to judge 'priced' when the only bar is a stale snippet.
